outputs.summary: Completed the scaling study for osu_allreduce from 1 to 5 nodes. The Flux Operator was installed on an ARM-based EKS cluster, and MiniClusters were created to run the benchmark at each scale. Latency data (FOM) was collected from the logs at each step, although data for the 2-node run was missed due to a pod retrieval issue.

results.reasons: The scaling study of the MPI Allreduce collective operation shows an expected trend in latency. For small message sizes, the latency increases with the number of nodes (and total processes) due to the overhead of establishing communication across more endpoints. For larger message sizes (e.g., > 65536 bytes), the latency continues to increase, but not always linearly, as the cost of data transfer and the reduction computation itself become the dominant factors. The use of AWS EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter) is critical in this environment to provide low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnect, which helps mitigate the network overhead that would otherwise be much more pronounced in a standard TCP/IP-based cloud environment. The observed behavior is consistent with performance models of collective operations in high-performance computing clusters.
results.citations: OSU Micro-Benchmarks, https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/benchmarks/; Thakur, R., Gropp, W., & Lusk, E. (2005). An experimental study of communication performance of MPI programs on three parallel computers. Parallel Computing, 31(8-9), 873-893.
